{{Current events|year=2019|month=02|day=02|content=
<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks

*[[Moro conflict]]
**[[Patikul, Sulu shootout]]
***Five soldiers and three militants die in an attack that also injured several others in [[Patikul, Sulu]], in The [[Philippines]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/02/philippine-army-deadly-battle-abu-sayyaf-jolo-blast-190202141556484.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Sistan and Baluchestan insurgency]]
**An [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps|Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] member is killed and five others are injured at an Iranian [[paramilitary]] base in [[Nik Shahr]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/02/attack-paramilitary-base-iran-holds-revolution-anniversary-190202064743401.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Somali Civil War]]
**Two people are killed and at least five others injured by a [[suicide car bombing]] that targeted an [[African Union]] Mission base in [[Somalia]]. [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]] claims responsibility for the attack. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/al-shabaab-attack-in-sw-somalia-kills-3-wounds-5/1382053 (AA)]

;Art and culture
*[[33rd Goya Awards]]
**The 33rd edition of [[Goya Awards]] are held in [[Seville]], [[Spain]]. ''[[Champions (2018 film)|Champions]]'', portrayed by disabled people, gets the [[Goya Award for Best Film]]. [https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/goya-awards-winners-list-1182141 (''Hollywood Reporter'')] [https://www.washingtonpost.com/entertainment/film-featuring-disabled-actors-wins-spains-top-goya-award/2019/02/03/32f1049c-27ab-11e9-906e-9d55b6451eb4_story.html (''Washington Post'')]

;Law and crime
*[[Crime in Cincinnati]]
**A sheriff's deputy is killed and another wounded during a 12 hour standoff in [[Cincinnati, Ohio]], United States. The suspect has been taken into custody. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/deputy-killed-another-wounded-after-12-hour-stand-n966326 (NBC News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*A collapse of a building [[Battle of Aleppo (2012–2016)|damaged by the war]] in [[Aleppo]], [[Syria]], kills 11 people. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-47103109 (BBC)]

;International relations
*[[Russia–United States relations]], [[Cold War II]]
**[[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] suspends Russia's involvement in the [[Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty]], and will now start developing new missiles, in response to the [[United States]]' decision to withdraw from the [[Cold War]]-era treaty. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-47101429 (BBC)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Crisis in Venezuela]], [[2019 Venezuelan presidential crisis]]
**Venezuela's [[Nicolás Maduro]] supports a proposal by the [[2017 Constituent National Assembly]] to hold [[Next Venezuelan parliamentary election|early legislative elections]], which is seen as an attempt to eliminate the threat posed by the [[Democratic Unity Roundtable|opposition]]-controlled [[National Assembly (Venezuela)|National Assembly]]. [[Vice President of the United States|U.S. Vice President]] [[Mike Pence]] tells a [[Florida]] rally that the time for dialogue "had ended" and "all options were on the table." [https://www.rte.ie/news/world/2019/0202/1027078-venezuela/ (RTE)]
**[[Venezuelan Air Force]] general Francisco Yáñez becomes the first high-ranking general to publicly support [[Juan Guaidó]] after he denounced the "dictatorship" of Maduro and recognized Guaidó's claim as the nation's legitimate leader. [https://www.foxnews.com/world/top-venezuela-general-rejects-maduros-legitimacy-throws-support-behind-interim-president (Fox News)]
**Hundreds of thousands of Venezuelan people take to the streets to protest socio-economic and political situation of the country and to demand a better economic situation. Large competing anti-Maduro and anti-Guaidó rallies are held in [[Caracas]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/the_americas/venezuela-protests-guaido-vs-maduro/2019/02/02/ef043b00-2660-11e9-b5b4-1d18dfb7b084_story.html?utm_term=.887de157eb3d (The Washington Post)]
* [[2019 Virginia political crisis]]
** [[Governor of Virginia|Governor]] of the U.S. state of [[Virginia]] [[Ralph Northam]] says he will not resign from office because he does not believe that he appears in a controversial photograph from his 1984 medical school [[yearbook]] showing one person wearing [[blackface]] and another person wearing [[Ku Klux Klan]] attire. However, Northam later admits to wearing blackface during the same time period for a dance contest, in order to imitate musician [[Michael Jackson]]. [https://www.postandcourier.com/politics/va-gov-ralph-northam-says-he-won-t-resign-denying/article_70e61994-2725-11e9-aed6-87235b6577f8.html?fbclid=IwAR3Gfo3KxT0burB3DzaqDJhJFKjb8hAaZZSG-hsPpWcQeAmTXrQKROPbKXM (''Post and Courier'')] [https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/northam-says-he-did-wear-blackface-but-not-in-racist-yearbook-photo?fbclid=IwAR3zb8shDREXRWQjnoZPcZshTuEw6srfofae2QZ64DyR51OYevarIEfZvec (''The Washington Examiner'')]
